Q1: Copper(I) iodide exhibits several known hazards (Tier 1) based on GHS classifications for environmental, oral, dermal/eye, and organ/systemic toxicity. It also shows expanded potential hazards (Tier 2) for carcinogenicity/mutagenicity/reproductive and inhalation concerns. Data for endocrine disruption potential, however, is currently deficient (Tier 4).
Q2: Copper(I) iodide appears on both the EPA's "Substances Added to Food" inventory and the FDA's "GRAS (Generally Recognized As Safe) list," indicating it is generally considered of low concern, especially in food-related applications.
Q3: This chemical is very well-characterized, boasting 22,000 literature references, significantly higher than the median for similar substances, and has a well-defined molecular structure. While it has not undergone full IRIS or PPRTV evaluations, it has a good number of toxicological records (30), with only endocrine disruption lacking sufficient data.
